report.source_text: The patient, therefore, underwent umbilectomy, excision of umbilical endometriosis, lysis of adhesions and umbilical hernia repair under general anaesthesia. A circumferential incision was made around the umbilicus using a scalpel. This was taken down to the subcutaneous tissue using electrocautery. The endometrioma was densely adherent to the umbilical skin as expected, as well as the hernia sac, the omental fat contents of the umbilical hernia sac and the anterior rectus sheath (see figure 3). This lesion was hence excised en masse with a wide margin, resulting in a large defect in the anterior abdominal wall (see figure 4). The defect was closed primarily using synthetic mesh and the skin edges were approximated using staples, leaving a subcutaneous drain (see figure 5). The specimen was sent to pathology for analysis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Surgical pathology revealed cystic endometriosis within subcutaneous tissue, consistent with umbilical endometrioma.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A nulliparous woman in her 40s with history of uterine fibroids and two abdominal myomectomies presented with umbilical pain and bleeding timed with menses. Physical exam revealed a 3 cm blood-filled cyst at the umbilicus consistent with umbilical endometriosis. MRI imaging confirmed the presence of an umbilical endometrioma. Medical therapy with medroxyprogesterone acetate was trialed without symptom relief. Surgical excision of the umbilical lesion (umbilectomy) was performed, with en masse removal of the lesion adherent to the umbilical skin, hernia sac, omental fat, and anterior rectus sheath, and abdominal wall mesh repair. While no strict safe excerpt of the surgical pathology report was available, it was documented that surgical pathology revealed cystic endometriosis within the subcutaneous tissue consistent with umbilical endometrioma, confirming the diagnosis.
